neighbours.label: verb or preposition describing how a held object or instrument is positioned (holding X out, something at the tip, from one hand to the other); weak and unclear
fire: “Stay back,” the guard warned, holding his torch out toward the dark mouth of the cave.
The dancer froze in the spotlight, holding her arms out like the wings of a bird.
The endoscope is a long thin cable with a tiny lens at the tip that the doctor feeds into the stomach.
The knight caught the reins, then passed the lance from his left hand to his right.
The beggar knelt by the gate, holding his bowl out to every stranger who passed.
The dentist uses a slender metal rod with a small mirror at the end to look behind the teeth.
The juggler tossed the club from one hand to the other without looking down.
“Take it,” the old woman said, holding the lantern out so that he could see the path.
quiet: “Stay back,” the guard warned, and the travellers waited quietly outside the cave.
The dancer froze in the spotlight while the music faded into silence.
The doctor explained that the stomach exam would take about twenty minutes.
The knight caught the reins and rode slowly toward the village gate.
The beggar knelt by the gate and sang to every stranger who passed.
The dentist looked at the chart and said the teeth were healthy.
The juggler bowed to the crowd and walked off the stage.
“Take it easy,” the old woman said, since the path was long and steep.
